# CrowdPlaySDK

> Swift package for iOS (17+) that records studio-grade per-participant
> audio (48 kHz / 24-bit WAV, unprocessed) and 1080p30 HEVC video LOCALLY
> on each participant's device during a live video call, time-aligns every
> participant's recording on a shared clock (millisecond accuracy), and
> uploads everything to CrowdPlay automatically. The integrating app makes ~5
> calls; capture, clock sync, consent evidence, upload, retry, and crash
> recovery all happen inside the SDK.

This file is the complete integration contract for an AI coding agent.
Follow it exactly. When this file and your instincts disagree, this file
wins.

## The mental model (read first)

Two media paths run at once and must never be confused:
- PATH A, the live call: LiveKit/WebRTC streams compressed audio/video
  between participants so they can talk. Deliberately low quality
  (default 640x360@24, 500 kbps video, 32 kbps Opus). Nothing from this
  path is kept.
- PATH B, the recording: each device records ITS OWN microphone and camera
  from the hardware at full quality, writes to local disk, uploads after.
  This is the product. It is unaffected by network quality, call quality
  settings, or what other participants do.

Consequences an agent must internalize:
- A bad network makes the CALL ugly; the RECORDING stays perfect.
- Each device records only its own participant. A 3-person call produces
  3 uploads that CrowdPlay's backend aligns into one session.
- Recording starts automatically on join() and stops on leave(). There is
  no separate record button to build.

## The HOST APP is the product — not recording

The builder came to you with an app idea (a tutoring app, a language-
exchange app, a remote interview tool…). Build THAT app. The SDK records
its video calls invisibly in the background; recording is infrastructure,
not identity:

- The app's NAME, description, onboarding, and screens are about the
  builder's idea. Never name or describe the app around recording
  ("lossless recorder", "records and stores your calls" — wrong).
- Recording surfaces in the UI in exactly three places: the consent
  screen before joining a call (required), a small REC indicator during
  the call, and join/leave. That is the whole visible footprint.
- Do NOT build: upload-progress screens, diagnostics/doctor screens, SDK
  settings pages, recording libraries or playback. Uploads run
  automatically in the background (they even run during the call);
  doctor() is a development-time check you run yourself, not a screen.
- After leave(), at most show one quiet line ("finishing up…") if uploads
  are still trailing; do not build a dedicated upload screen unless the
  builder explicitly asks.
- If the builder's instruction mentions only "video calls", still use
  this SDK exactly as specified here — consent included. Consent is the
  one recording-related UI that must never be minimized away.

## Hard rules (violations corrupt recordings or break builds)

1. CrowdPlaySDK is the ONLY package you add and `import CrowdPlaySDK` the ONLY
   import you write. CrowdPlaySDK re-exports everything, including the LiveKit
   call-UI types (SwiftUIVideoView, RemoteParticipant, Room). NEVER add,
   pin, import, or update LiveKit or WebRTC yourself — the correct version
   ships inside CrowdPlaySDK, matched to the capture engine. Adding your own
   causes duplicate-symbol build failures or, worse, a version mismatch
   that silently breaks capture.
2. NEVER write AVAudioSession, AVAudioEngine, AVCaptureSession, or
   AVAudioRecorder code in an app using CrowdPlaySDK. The SDK owns the
   microphone and the camera, and iOS allows only one owner. Touching them
   — even "harmlessly" setting a category — corrupts the recording.
3. NEVER skip, fake, or auto-dismiss the consent step. join() requires a
   ConsentRecord (non-optional parameter — the compiler enforces it) and
   the user must actually SEE the consent text before you mint one.
   Constructing ConsentRecord(givenAt: Date()) without showing
   CrowdPlayConsent.text to the user creates false legal evidence.
4. NEVER call the microphone/camera before Info.plist has
   NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSCameraUsageDescription. iOS kills
   the app instantly (not an exception you can catch).
5. Test on a REAL iPhone. The Simulator has no camera or microphone;
   recording code paths cannot be exercised there at all.

## Integration procedure

### Step 1 — add the package

Xcode: File > Add Package Dependencies > paste this repository's URL >
add product "CrowdPlaySDK" to the app target. The package resolves a compiled
binary (CrowdPlaySDKCore) plus a thin source shim; no other setup.

### Step 2 — Info.plist

    NSMicrophoneUsageDescription = "Records your microphone during sessions."
    NSCameraUsageDescription     = "Records your camera during sessions."
    UIBackgroundModes            = [audio]

UIBackgroundModes audio keeps capture alive if the app is briefly
backgrounded and lets uploads finish after the call.

### Step 3 — configure at launch

    import CrowdPlaySDK

    // In App.init() or application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:):
    CrowdPlay.configure(CrowdPlayConfiguration(
        serverURL: URL(string: "https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai")!,
        appKey: "<the builder's liva_pk_… key from the CrowdPlay dashboard>"
    ))

configure() is also the crash-recovery hook: it resumes any uploads
interrupted by a crash, reboot, or dead battery. Call it exactly once,
before any other SDK use (using the SDK unconfigured is a deliberate
preconditionFailure with a clear message).

Optional CrowdPlayConfiguration fields (defaults are hardware-proven; change
only when asked to):

    uploadsEnabled: Bool = true          // false = recordings stay on device (dev only)
    deleteAfterUpload: Bool = true       // local files removed only AFTER S3 acknowledges
    videoUploadsOnCellular: Bool = false // audio+manifests always upload on any network;
                                         // video (~2 GB/session) waits for WiFi unless true
    uploadDuringCall: Bool = true        // segments upload WHILE recording (one at a
                                         // time, auto-paused when call quality drops),
                                         // so the post-call wait is ~the final segment
    requiredFreeDiskBytes: Int64 = 8 GB  // join() refuses below this
    remoteAudioGain: Double = 1.0        // playout gain; >1.0 increases cross-talk bleed
    logSessionsTreeAtLaunch: Bool = false
    callQuality: CallQuality             // PATH A ONLY, see below

CallQuality (live call appearance; the recording is always full quality
regardless): videoWidth/videoHeight (default 640x360, clamped
160x90…1280x720), videoFps (24, clamped 10…30), videoBitrate (500_000,
clamped 100k…2.5M), audioBitrate (32_000, clamped 16k…128k). Raising these
costs uplink bandwidth and thermal headroom that the recording needs on
long sessions — leave defaults unless the builder explicitly wants a
prettier live picture.

### Step 4 — background upload hook

    // UIApplicationDelegate:
    func application(_ application: UIApplication,
                     handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession identifier: String,
                     completionHandler: @escaping () -> Void) {
        CrowdPlay.handleBackgroundURLSessionEvents(completionHandler: completionHandler)
    }

Without this, iOS eventually stops delivering background-upload events to
the app and post-call uploads stall until next launch.

### Step 5 — consent, then join

    @StateObject private var engine = CallEngine()   // one per app

    // The drop-in consent screen (recommended):
    CrowdPlayConsentView { consent in
        Task { await engine.join(displayName: name, roomCode: code, consent: consent) }
    }

    // OR custom consent UI — MUST display CrowdPlayConsent.text verbatim, then:
    let consent = ConsentRecord(givenAt: Date())

roomCode is any string the participants share (like a meeting ID); everyone
who joins with the same code lands in the same call and the same aligned
session. It is normalized internally (trimmed, filesystem-safe), so
user-typed codes with stray spaces are fine.

Tip: call CrowdPlay.warmUp() when the join screen appears — it pre-warms the
backend connection so joining is faster.

### Step 6 — build the call UI from engine state

CallEngine is an ObservableObject. Published state:

    engine.phase                // .idle / .connecting / .connected / .failed(String)
    engine.isRecording          // true while capturing
    engine.isMicMuted
    engine.isCameraEnabled
    engine.recordingStartError  // String?; NON-NIL MEANS THE SESSION IS NOT
                                // BEING RECORDED. Show it prominently and
                                // offer engine.retryRecording(displayName:).
    engine.uploads              // [UploadManager.Progress] — per-session upload
                                //   progress: .fraction (0…1), .isComplete,
                                //   .bytesUploaded/.bytesTotal, .video (per-kind),
                                //   .isFinishedWithFailures (offer retryUploads())
    engine.uploadsOnWiFi        // false = video is waiting for WiFi; say so in UI
    engine.crossTalkRisk        // true = far-end audio is leaking into the mic
                                //   (loudspeaker use) — tell the user to wear headphones
    engine.headphonesConnected
    engine.currentOutputName    // e.g. "AirPods Pro" — for a route indicator
    engine.room                 // the live Room: engine.room.remoteParticipants
                                //   for rendering video tiles

Render remote video tiles with the re-exported SwiftUIVideoView:

    ForEach(Array(engine.room.remoteParticipants.values), id: \.identity) { p in
        if let track = p.firstCameraVideoTrack {
            SwiftUIVideoView(track)
        }
    }
    // Self view: engine.room.localParticipant.firstCameraVideoTrack,
    // rendered with SwiftUIVideoView(track, mirrorMode: .mirror).

Poll engine.recordingSnapshot() at ~1 Hz for the REC indicator; it returns
seconds recorded, segments closed, droppedSamples, inputLevelDbfs,
inputSilent (mic delivering silence — dead mic), audioStalled (capture
stalled, self-healing in progress), fullScaleSamples (clipping). Surface
inputSilent / audioStalled / clipping as visible warnings — they mean the
data being captured right now is degraded and the user can often fix it
(replug mic, move phone).

### Step 7 — controls

    await engine.toggleMute()   // mutes the CALL and writes SILENCE to the
                                // recording (never secretly records a muted user)
    engine.toggleCamera()       // black frames on both paths; timeline continuous
    await engine.leave()        // stops recording; uploads start automatically

After leave(), uploads finish automatically in the background — most
already went out during the call. Show at most one quiet line ("finishing
up…") while `engine.uploads` has an incomplete entry; do NOT build a
dedicated upload screen (see "The HOST APP is the product"). Force-
quitting pauses uploads until next launch (nothing is lost; they resume).

Advanced (only when the builder asks): engine.micOptions +
selectMicrophone(_:) (built-in / wired / external mic policy; Bluetooth
mics are deliberately excluded — HFP drops the whole session to 16 kHz),
engine.selectOutput(_:) (speaker vs automatic), engine.sessionMode.

### Step 8 — verify

    let checks = await CrowdPlay.doctor()   // [DoctorCheck(id, passed, detail)]

Doctor checks: configured, Info.plist strings, mic+camera permission,
free disk, backend reachable, app key authenticates. Every failing check's
detail names its own fix. NOTE: on a fresh install the "permissions" check
reports "not requested yet — NORMAL"; that is the expected pre-first-run
state (iOS prompts at first join), not an integration bug — do not hunt
for one. Only a DENIED state needs action (the user re-enables in
Settings). Fix everything actionable, then move to Step 9.

### Step 9 — hand off to the builder (REQUIRED final message)

The Simulator has no camera or microphone, so NOTHING you built can be
validated until it runs on a real iPhone. Do not end with "the
implementation is complete" — your FINAL message after implementing must
walk the builder through their next step, explicitly:

1. Plug an iPhone into the Mac; tap "Trust This Computer" on the phone.
   First time only: Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode > ON
   (the phone restarts).
2. In Xcode: Signing & Capabilities > pick a Team (a free Personal Team
   works); select the iPhone in the device menu; press Run. If the phone
   says "Untrusted Developer": Settings > General > VPN & Device
   Management > Trust, then Run again.
3. In the app: allow microphone + camera when prompted, join any room
   code, talk for about a minute, then leave.
4. Check https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai — the session appears there with
   its recording; that is the proof the integration works end to end.

## Accessing recordings (no AWS, no SDK — plain HTTPS)

The app key doubles as the data credential:

    GET https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai/sessions
        header x-liva-key: <app key>
        -> [{sessionId, state ("uploading"|"ok"|"partial"|"failed"),
             participants, warnings, uploadedAt}]

    GET https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai/sessions/<sessionId>/files
        header x-liva-key: <app key>
        -> [{path, bytes, url}]   // url = 1-hour presigned download

deliverable/ is what a consumer uses: speaker-<name>.wav per participant
(48 kHz/24-bit, drift-corrected — all files play together with NO offset),
conversation.wav (mixed), conversation_stereo.wav (2-person),
alignment.json, qc.json (quality verdict). raw/ is the untouched
per-device capture. A key can only see its own app's sessions. Humans use
the same data via https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai (sign in, click, download).

## Facts, limits, troubleshooting

- iOS 17+, Swift 5.10+. Ships LiveKit (exact-pinned) + swift-atomics inside.
- Storage: ~2 GB per participant-hour (video-dominated). join() refuses
  below 8 GB free (configurable).
- Keep the screen awake in sessions: view.onAppear
  { UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled = true } (and false on leave).
  There is no CallKit integration; a locked phone suspends capture.
- Participants should wear wired or closed-back headphones. Loudspeaker
  playback leaks the far end into the local mic (crossTalkRisk warns live).
- Interruptions (phone call, Siri, route change, reconnect) are survived:
  capture watchdogs force-restart a stalled engine within ~3 s and every
  event is logged into the session manifest with timestamps.
- Slow join or glitchy first seconds of a recording = poor radio
  environment (congested 2.4 GHz WiFi + Bluetooth share the antenna) or
  the Xcode debugger attached — NOT an integration bug. Capture self-heals
  once the link settles. Advise: better network, wired headphones, launch
  from the home screen when evaluating quality.
- "unauthorized"/401 from the backend: the app key is wrong — sign in at
  https://dashboard.crowdplay.ai, reveal the key, and copy it again.
- Uploads crawling on an otherwise-fine network: check for a VPN, iCloud
  Private Relay, or Low Data Mode on the phone. A VPN can cut upload
  throughput 100×, and Low Data Mode marks WiFi "expensive," which makes
  video wait forever for real WiFi. Verified in the field: turning the
  VPN off took one phone from ~1 Mbps to full line rate.
- Build error "duplicate symbol"/"multiple commands produce" mentioning
  LiveKit or WebRTC: the app added its own LiveKit dependency — remove it
  (rule 1).
- App crashes instantly on join: missing Info.plist usage description
  (rule 4). doctor() catches this.

Reference integration: Examples/CrowdPlaySample in this repository — a
complete consent -> join -> record -> upload app in ~150 lines. Prefer
copying its structure over inventing one.
Human-readable docs: README.md. Zero-experience walkthrough: GETTING_STARTED.md.
